chapters.title: Elders for Crete
chapters.html:
Titus 1

1Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, for the faith of God's chosen ones and their knowledge of the truth that accords with godliness,

2in hope of eternal life, which God, who cannot lie, promised before the ages began,

3and at the proper time revealed His word in the preaching entrusted to me by command of God our Savior,

4to Titus, my true son in our common faith: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.

Elders

5This is why I left you in Crete: so that you might put in order what remained to be done and appoint elders in every town as I directed you,

6if anyone is above reproach, the husband of one wife, with believing children who are not open to the charge of wild living or disobedience.

7For an overseer, as God's steward, must be above reproach. He must not be arrogant or quick-tempered or a drunkard or violent or greedy for gain,

8but hospitable, a lover of good, self-controlled, upright, holy and disciplined,

9holding firm to the trustworthy word as taught, so that he may be able both to encourage with sound teaching and to rebuke those who contradict it.

Silencing the Deceivers

10For there are many who are insubordinate, empty talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision.

11They must be silenced, for they are upsetting whole households by teaching what they ought not, for the sake of shameful gain.

12One of them, a prophet of their own, said, "Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons."

13This testimony is true. So rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in the faith,

14not giving their minds to Jewish myths and the commandments of people who turn away from the truth.

15To the pure all things are pure, but to the defiled and unbelieving nothing is pure; both their minds and their consciences are defiled.

16They claim to know God, but by their works they deny Him. They are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.

chapters.title: Sound Teaching
chapters.html:
Titus 2

1But as for you, teach what fits sound teaching.

2Older men are to be sober-minded, dignified, self-controlled, sound in faith, in love and in endurance.

3Older women likewise are to be reverent in behavior, not slanderers or slaves to much wine. They are to teach what is good,

4and so train the young women to love their husbands and children,

5to be self-controlled, pure, working at home, kind, and submissive to their own husbands, so that the word of God may not be blasphemed.

6Likewise urge the younger men to be self-controlled.

7Show yourself in all respects a model of good works, and in your teaching show integrity and dignity,

8and sound speech that cannot be condemned, so that an opponent may be put to shame, having nothing bad to say about us.

9Slaves are to be submissive to their own masters in everything, to please them and not talk back,

10not stealing, but showing all good faith, so that in everything they may adorn the teaching of God our Savior.

The Grace of God Has Appeared

11For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people,

12training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly desires, and to live self-controlled, upright and godly lives in the present age,

13waiting for the blessed hope, the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior Jesus Christ,

14who gave Himself for us to redeem us from all lawlessness and to purify for Himself a people for His own possession, zealous for good works.

15Speak these things, and urge and rebuke with all authority. Let no one disregard you.

Notes

  • v13 "our great God and Savior Jesus Christ" — tou megalou theou kai sōtēros hēmōn Iēsou Christou, with one article over both nouns, which in Greek usually makes them one person: Jesus Christ is our great God and Savior. It can also be read as two, the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ.

  • v14 "a people for His own possession" — laon periousion, the words of Sinai, you will be My own treasure out of all the peoples (Exodus 19:5), laos periousios in the Greek. What God said to Israel at the mountain is said here of the people Christ purifies for Himself.

chapters.title: The Washing of Rebirth
chapters.html:
Titus 3

Saved by His Mercy

1Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,

2to speak evil of no one, to avoid quarreling, to be gentle, and to show every courtesy to all people.

3For we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, led astray, slaves to all kinds of desires and pleasures, living our days in malice and envy, hateful and hating one another.

4But when the kindness and love for mankind of God our Savior appeared,

5He saved us, not because of works done by us in righteousness, but according to His own mercy, through the washing of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit,

6whom He poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior,

7so that, being justified by His grace, we might become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

8The saying is trustworthy, and I want you to insist on these things, so that those who have believed in God may be careful to devote themselves to good works. These things are good and useful for people.

9But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, strife and quarrels about the Law, for they are useless and empty.

10Warn a divisive person once and then twice, and after that have nothing more to do with him,

11knowing that such a person is warped and sinful; he is self-condemned.

Final Instructions

12When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, do your best to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to spend the winter there.

13Do your best to speed Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way; see that they lack nothing.

14Let our people also learn to devote themselves to good works, to meet pressing needs, so that they may not be unfruitful.

15All who are with me greet you. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all.
